critical_issues: Medium: The lower cloth area feels physically implausible relative to the ground, suggesting dragging or clipping risk.
warnings: Line 160: Reduce world background strength from 0.8 to roughly 0.2-0.4 to avoid the washed-out look, then rely more on a dedicated sun key light from above-right for stronger shadow direction.

Lines 396-397: Tune the cloth shader away from flat overbright white; try Base Color around 0.92-0.95 instead of 0.97 and Roughness around 0.55-0.65 instead of 0.72 so cotton keeps softness but gains better form definition.
Lines 346-347: Shift the mixed cloth colors toward a cleaner warm white and reduce the gray-green cast so the sheet reads as sunlit cotton rather than dull placeholder fabric.
Lines 406-407: Make weave detail more readable by lowering weave_noise Scale from 160 to about 100-120 and increasing Detail from 3 to about 5-6.
Lines 410-411: For broader surface breakup, lower soft_noise Scale from 7 to about 3-5 and consider Detail around 4-5; current surface detail is too uniform.
If Lines 369-370 drive visible cloth surface patterning, try lowering wave Scale from 40 to about 18-25 and raising Distortion from 1.4 to about 2.0-3.0 for more readable fabric variation.
Line 460: If this BSDF controls posts or clothespins, Metallic should not be 1.0; set it near 0.0 because the current value likely makes hard-surface materials look synthetic.
Line 481: If this Base Color belongs to posts/clothespins, replace the near-gray color with a warmer wood tone so those objects read as weathered wood instead of plain cylinders.

Main issue is simulation, not just shading: expose and increase wind strength variation/turbulence, improve cloth substeps/collision quality, and strengthen pin constraints so the sheet develops sharper billows, layered ripples, and snap-like tension near attachment points.
Add clear visible wooden clothespins and a more believable backyard context; shader tweaks alone will not raise this to pass quality.
